title: A Failed Ointment Venture, a Brother's Push and Kalbe's Garage
dek: After his first drug venture closed, Boenjamin Setiawan and his siblings pooled their money in 1966 and started Kalbe Farma in a Jakarta garage.

story.event: Starting Kalbe Farma in a North Jakarta garage after an earlier venture failed
story.summary: Boenjamin Setiawan, a University of Indonesia medical graduate trained in pharmacology in the United States, was told in 1961 that research of the kind he wanted needed a drug company behind it. An ointment venture he started with friends in 1963 closed for lack of money and sales. On 10 September 1966 he and his siblings, pooling their own money, founded Kalbe Farma in a garage in North Jakarta; he led it until 2008.
paragraphs: In 1961, by his own account, Boenjamin Setiawan came home from studies in the United States with a plan for research, not a business. A doctor who had qualified at the University of Indonesia in 1958 and would hold a doctorate in pharmacology from the University of California, he went to Wim Kalona, owner of the drug firm PT Dupa, and asked for Rp30 million to study herbal remedies for diabetes and high blood pressure. Kalona's answer, Setiawan told an audience at the University of Indonesia in 2015, was that if he wanted to do research he would have to build a pharmaceutical company. Setiawan said he had never set out to dream of one.

His first attempt failed. In 1963 he and a few friends, all under thirty as he remembered it, began making ointment on Sundays, in a venture later reports call PT Farmindo. It ran short of money and struggled to sell what it made; one account adds that it was not run professionally. After about three years it closed.

He tried again, this time with family. His elder brother, a dentist, urged him to keep going with the idea of a drug factory, and a sister was also a doctor. The siblings pooled their own money, and on 10 September 1966 they founded Kalbe Farma, its name, he said, a reworking of KLB, the initials he shared with his brother Khouw Lip Bing. They started not in a factory but in a garage in North Jakarta that belonged to a patient, of his brother's in his telling and of his own in another account.

He told the same audience that a garage was no bad place to begin: starting from hardship, he said, made people keener to succeed. He led Kalbe from its founding until 2008, when his niece, Irawati Setiady, became president director. In the 1998 financial crisis, when the rupiah fell from about 3,000 to 15,000 to the dollar, the company cut costs to avoid layoffs and renegotiated its debts with 35 banks. By 2021 it employed about 17,000 people. Setiawan died in April 2023.

quote.text: If you see an intelligent man who tells you where true treasures are to be found, who shows what is to be avoided, and administers reproofs, follow that wise man; it will be better, not worse, for those who follow him.
quote.source_title: Dhammapada, a Collection of Verses, tr. F. Max Müller, Project Gutenberg eBook #2017
quote.connection: The verse asks us to follow the person who shows where the treasure lies and tells us plainly what to avoid. Setiawan's story has two such people: a businessman who told him research needed a company, and a brother who told him to try again after the first one failed.

reflection: Two pieces of advice turned Setiawan's path, and neither was what he had asked for. He wanted research money and was told to build a company. When his first company closed, he could have taken that as the answer. His brother told him to try again, and the family put in their own money.

There may be someone who has told you something unwelcome about your work, or who believes in it more steadily than you do this week. It helps to decide whose judgement you trust before the hard days come, so that on those days you are not choosing by mood. Advice heard at the end of a long, tired day is rarely heard well.
invitation: Think of one person whose honest advice has proved right before. Send them a short message today about the piece of work you feel least sure of, and ask them one question about it.

research_notes: Sources are Indonesian-language except Forbes; his words are paraphrased in English, not quoted. The 1961 Kalona request: detik (quoting his 30 October 2015 Tanoto Foundation talk) and CNN Indonesia give Rp30 million for research on herbal remedies for diabetes and blood pressure, with Kalona telling him research meant founding a company (CNN says Kalona refused); CNBC Indonesia instead describes a cheap skin-medicine research project costing Rp1.5 million that Kalona, though shocked at the cost, agreed to support. The story follows Setiawan's own account and attributes it to his 2015 talk. The first venture: detik (his words) says only that young friends made ointment on Sundays and it closed when capital ran out; CNN says PT Farmindo, founded in 1963, lasted about three years and closed for lack of capital and marketing problems; CNBC says it failed because it was not run professionally; all three reasons are given. The site: a workshop (bengkel) owned by a patient of his elder brother (detik, CNN, his own telling) against the garage of a house in Tanjung Priok rented from one of his own patients (CNBC); the story says a garage in North Jakarta and gives both versions of whose patient. Founders: 'five siblings' (Forbes), 'five colleagues' (Kontan), and CNN names Khouw Lip Keng, Khouw Lip Swan and Khouw Lip Bing plus a pharmacologist friend, Jan Tan; detik has Setiawan mentioning a dentist brother and a doctor sister; the story says 'the siblings' without a number. His age at death is given as 89 (Forbes) and 80 (CNN Indonesia, 2023), and his birth year as 1933 (CNN Indonesia, 2021) and 1943 (detik); no age is used. The year of his doctorate is not given in the sources, so the story does not say he held it by 1961. First products differ (Bioplacenton per CNN; syrups, drops and capsules per CNBC) and are omitted. Detik's passage also mentions a plan to go to the Netherlands that is grammatically unclear about who would have gone; it is omitted. Name: Wikipedia (not cited) says Kalbe abbreviates Khouw Lip Boen alone; CNBC quotes Setiawan saying the initials KLB stood for him and his brother Khouw Lip Bing, and the story follows him. The founding date of 10 September 1966 comes from CNBC Indonesia (and Wikipedia, not cited). The verse is general counsel to follow wise teachers; it is applied here to two advisers by analogy.
